newsitem.title: USA: Major U.S. airlines surpass Q1 expectations.
newsitem.headline: Major U.S. airlines surpass Q1 expectations.

text.p: U.S. airlines' earnings topped Wall Street expectations as strong demand, higher air fares and controlled capacity growth offset rising fuel prices, analysts said.

UAL Corp, AMR Corp, Continental Airlines Inc and Northwest Airlines Corp each beat analysts' consensus earnings estimates. Even Trans World Airlines Inc, which posted a $71.6 million first quarter loss, had a better-than-expected quarter.

"Overall, the strength in revenues surpassed our expectations and the Street expectations. We see the strength in demand continuing for the next quarter," said Susan Donofrio, an analyst with NatWest Securities.

The airlines' revenues surpassed expectations even though the carriers enjoyed the benefit of the lapse in the passenger excise tax for only part of the first quarter. Last year, the tax was absent for eight months.
Donofrio said she was pleasantly surprised by UAL and AMR's strong showing and expects Delta Air Lines Inc to continue the trend when it reports its third fiscal quarter results on Thursday.
UAL, owner of United Airlines, posted first quarter earnings of $1.61 per fully distributed share, shattering Wall Street estimates of $1.40 a share.

UAL's shares jumped 3-1/2 to 78-3/8 in afternoon trading. UAL said its strong results were due mostly to continued domestic passenger unit revenue growth, while labor unrest at American Airlines "provided a modest benefit to the company."

AMR, owner of American Airlines, last week beat analysts expectations even though it posted a drop in first quarter profits compared with last year. AMR's first quarter results were hurt by its bitter labor dispute with its pilots and higher fuel and operating costs.

"American's performance in the March quarter was surprisingly strong given the operational chaos that the pilots negotiations and mini-strike caused," Dillon Read analyst Edward Starkman said in a recent research report.

Northwest Airlines said its strong domestic demand was offset by sharply higher fuel prices and a weakening yen. Northwest, the nation's fourth largest airline, said it expects the second quarter to be even more challenging than the first.
Despite Northwest's caution about the second quarter, some analysts said they may raise their second quarter estimates to account for strong demand.
But other analysts cautioned that too much weight is being placed on Wall Street earnings estimates.
The consensus forecast is often overly cautious and its viewed more as as the "worst case scenario," instead of an accurate gauge of earnings potential, analysts said.
The Dow Jones transportation average jumped almost 47 points or 1.88 percent to 2523 in afternoon trading, while the Dow Jones industrials gained 122 points to 6783.
